claims.statement: For a finite, non-explosive CTMC with common initial law and transition rates q_theta(x,y)=theta*a(x,y) on a designated edge set, while all other rates are theta-independent, the complete path LLR is K*log(theta1/theta0)-(theta1-theta0)*A; its KL divergence is d_Pois(theta1||theta0)*E_theta1[A].
assumptions: Finite state space and no explosion on finite horizons
0 < theta0, theta1 < infinity and common transition support
Known, time-homogeneous baseline edge rates a(x,y)
Common initial law independent of the hypothesis
Complete path observation for the sufficiency statement
claims.status: internally proved conditional theorem; standard likelihood structure
claims.novelty_boundary: The likelihood factorization and data-processing step are standard. No priority claim; contribution is the explicit activity-normalized form for this sensor interface.

costs.activity: A_T=integral_0^T a(X_t)dt; assume A_T<=a_max*T for the horizon bound
costs.sufficient_statistic: current state, exact signal-transition count K_T, and integrated activity A_T
costs.precision: quantizing A_T to LLR error delta requires activity resolution <=2*delta/abs(theta1-theta0); K_T is unbounded absent a tail truncation
costs.acquisition: rate calibration and event/state sensing are not supplied by the theorem

claims.falsifier: A valid model within the stated assumptions whose complete-path LLR or relative entropy differs from the displayed formulas.
claims.next_gate: Extend the activity bound to hidden and controlled CTMC observations with charged policy and state information.

claims.statement: For a serial m-stage CTMC with hypothesis-independent forward rates k_i>0 and reset hazards mu0>mu1>0, endpoint success probabilities p_h=product_i k_i/(k_i+mu_h) satisfy p0>=p1^(mu0/mu1). At fixed m and p1, equal per-stage H1 success probabilities minimize p0; the finite-m optimum decreases to the power-law floor as m tends to infinity.
assumptions: One initial state, m serial forward transitions, and one absorbing reset outcome
At stage i the only outgoing transitions are forward at k_i and reset at mu_h
Forward rates do not depend on h; the reset hazard is the same at every stage within each hypothesis
Only terminal success/failure is used for the reported p_h
claims.status: internally proved conditional theorem; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Related multistage accuracy/speed/dissipation and first-passage/count analyses are established. This is a specific terminal-probability theorem at matched sensitivity; priority remains unverified.

costs.state_count: m+2 including reset and response terminals
costs.not_fixed: energy and rate calibration; at the equalized optimizer stage-event count and forward rate grow linearly in m

claims.falsifier: Within the stated CTMC interface, any rates and stage count yielding p0<p1^(mu0/mu1).
claims.next_gate: Generalize to multiple reset paths and determine sharp activity-constrained bounds.

claims.statement: If all signal-dependent CTMC rates depend on unknown gain gamma and input intensity u only through theta=gamma*u, then any rescaled pair (c*gamma,u/c) induces the same generator and path law; gamma and u are not separately identifiable from any trajectory statistic.
assumptions: Every transition rate is invariant under gamma*u-preserving rescaling
No independently calibrated gain or input measurement is supplied
claims.novelty_boundary: A basic structural identifiability gauge; no novelty claim.

costs.required_additional_information: independent gain/input calibration or a second transition channel with distinct parameter dependence

claims.falsifier: An observation law under the stated parameterization that changes when gamma*u is held fixed.
claims.next_gate: Quantify the minimum independent calibration needed when auxiliary channels are noisy.

claims.statement: For a known k-mode pure-death hidden CTMC with distinct positive decay rates and nonzero occupancy-times-effect amplitudes, 2k equally spaced exact terminal discrimination means identify unordered rate/amplitude pairs, but terminal delay data identify occupancy and per-mode effect only through their product.
assumptions: Known k and one absorbing baseline mode
Distinct positive decay rates and nonzero mode amplitudes
Terminal Bernoulli readouts at known delays; no hidden path observation
Reset baseline supplied or separately measured
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; classical Prony component
claims.novelty_boundary: Prony reconstruction and hidden-Markov identifiability are established. This exact occupancy/effect confounding is scoped to the terminal-probability observation map; no novelty claim.

costs.delay_points: 2k exact scalar means, span (2k-1)*h, plus reset baseline
costs.computation: O(k^3) arithmetic and O(k^2) storage; noise stability depends on mode separation and amplitudes
costs.extra_observable: labeled occupancy or calibrated p_r is required to separate occupancy from effect

claims.falsifier: A terminal-delay-only estimator that uniquely recovers occupancy and state-specific effect on an open parameter set under the stated model.
claims.next_gate: General transient subgenerator; characterize similarity-class ambiguity and noisy observability.

claims.statement: For the N+1-state chain with forward rate theta from i to i+1 for i<N and reset rate rho from i>0 to 0, the stationary full-path KL rate is [1-(theta1/(theta1+rho))^N]*d_Pois(theta1||theta0); N raises active exposure with geometric diminishing returns. A detector using only X_T after one long run has positive limiting error because the stationary endpoint distributions have full support.
assumptions: N >= 1 and theta0, theta1, rho > 0
Forward events are the only theta-sensitive transitions
Reset rate is hypothesis-independent
Complete timed path for the KL-rate claim; only terminal state X_T for the endpoint-only counterexample
claims.status: internally proved exact model special case and counterexample; no nature or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Stationary distribution and path-space KL specialization are elementary consequences of CTMC theory. The endpoint statement is limited to one terminal observation and does not rule out temporal accumulation.

costs.full_path: expected event count at most (theta1+rho)*T in the reset example; timestamps and labels cost extra precision/storage

claims.falsifier: An algebraic contradiction to the displayed stationary distribution or entropy rate under the stated generator.
claims.next_gate: Compare terminal and partial-time path readouts under explicit sampling intervals and event-record budgets.

claims.statement: For N iid Bernoulli event marks with common hypothesis-independent exponential event times, the all-pass terminal bit is a deterministic coarsening of the full mark path and has KL at most N*d_Ber(p0||p1), strictly less for N>=2 and p0!=p1. A finite stage-count CTMC with N(N+1)/2+2 states realizes the Neyman-Pearson threshold decision from N marks using one terminal bit at the same N jumps and mean time.
assumptions: Two known simple hypotheses; 0<p0,p1<1 and p0!=p1
Independent Bernoulli marks with the same p_h at every slot
Common hypothesis-independent Exp(lambda) event times
Fixed N and a terminal binary decision
claims.status: internally proved conditional comparison using data processing and Neyman-Pearson; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The information ordering and threshold optimality are classical; the report reconstructs their exact finite-stage CTMC costs and matched readout interface. No priority claim.

costs.all_pass: 2N+1 reachable states; N jumps; mean elapsed time N/lambda; one terminal readout
costs.likelihood_counter: N(N+1)/2+2 reachable states; N jumps; mean elapsed time N/lambda; one terminal readout
costs.raw_marks: N external mark observations and N+1 count values; KL ceiling N*d_Ber(p0||p1)

claims.falsifier: A violation of data processing or of the Neyman-Pearson threshold result within the stated iid Bernoulli model.
claims.next_gate: Characterize the state-cardinality versus observation-cost frontier for explicitly specified finite-state transducers.

claims.statement: For two finite-state CTMCs with common transition support, the full-path KL is the initial-law KL plus the integral of occupancy-weighted row divergences. Every common readout channel has no larger KL, and equal-prior binary error is at least exp(-D_T)/4. Hidden strong lumping and one-lag generator aliasing give exact observational-equivalence counterexamples.
assumptions: Finite non-explosive CTMCs on a common finite state space
Common edge support and initial absolute continuity
A common hypothesis-independent readout channel
The endpoint error bound is for equal priors
claims.status: internally proved conditional general CTMC formula and elementary counterexamples; established mechanisms; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The path likelihood, data-processing, and finite-state identifiability principles are established. Contributions are scoped formulas and exact counterexamples for explicit observation interfaces; external proof review and priority audit remain open.
